stories.title: US says they’re talking, Iran says they’re not. Who’s telling the truth?
stories.summary: US and Iranian officials have issued conflicting statements regarding whether negotiations between the two countries are taking place, with critics suggesting the US claim may be intended to stabilize markets.

stories.title: Egypt’s Mohamed Salah to leave Liverpool at end of season after 9-year stay
stories.summary: Egyptian forward Mohamed Salah will depart Liverpool Football Club at the conclusion of the current season after nine years with the Premier League champions, with reports linking him to a potential move to the Saudi Pro League.

stories.title: What impact is the war on Iran having on Israel?
stories.summary: Iranian missiles have struck Israeli territory as the ongoing conflict between the two nations contributes to broader global economic disruption.

stories.title: Why is Trump asking for Europe’s help in war on Iran?
stories.summary: Former French Ambassador to the US Gerard Araud has commented on President Trump's request for European assistance in the conflict with Iran, arguing that European nations are justified in staying out of the US-Israeli military campaign.

stories.title: Aid flotilla vessel arrives in Cuba amid US-driven energy crisis
stories.summary: An aid flotilla vessel has arrived in Cuba, with activists describing the delivery as a symbolic act of solidarity intended to highlight the impact of US sanctions on Cuba's energy supply.

stories.title: Russia launches 948 drones at Ukraine in largest attack over 24-hour period
stories.summary: Russia conducted its largest drone attack on Ukraine to date, launching 948 drones over a 24-hour period and striking cities across western Ukraine, damaging residential buildings and causing multiple injuries.

stories.title: Iran names successor to security chief killed in US-Israeli attack
stories.summary: Iran has appointed Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr, a former commander of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, to serve as chief of the Supreme National Security Council, replacing Ali Larijani who was killed in a US-Israeli attack.

stories.title: Israeli strike lands near Roman ruins in Lebanon
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike hit a building near the ancient Roman ruins in the Lebanese city of Tyre, with smoke visible rising close to the historic site.

stories.title: Anthropic challenges US Pentagon’s ban in San Francisco court showdown
stories.summary: Anthropic has filed a legal challenge against the US Pentagon in a San Francisco court, alleging the department unlawfully retaliated against the company for refusing to relax its AI safety restrictions for military applications.

stories.title: Israeli soldiers accused of ‘torturing’ toddler in Gaza
stories.summary: A family in Gaza has accused Israeli soldiers of torturing their two-year-old son in an attempt to obtain information about the child's father.

stories.title: Everyday life in Asia is being upended by Iran war fuel crisis
stories.summary: The ongoing conflict involving Iran is disrupting daily life across Asia, as the region's heavy dependence on Gulf oil and gas leads to fuel shortages and rising prices.

stories.title: Israel says it will take control of large buffer zone in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israel's defence minister announced plans to establish control over a large buffer zone in southern Lebanon, stating that displaced Lebanese residents will not be permitted to return until northern Israel is deemed secure.

stories.title: Palestinian FA calls for Israeli ban after FIFA discrimination report
stories.summary: The Palestinian Football Association has called for Israel's ban from international football after FIFA fined the Israel Football Association for racism and discrimination violations following a complaint filed by Palestinian officials.

stories.title: Israeli defences questioned as Iran continues to cause damage
stories.summary: Iranian missile strikes have inflicted damage on Israeli targets, prompting questions about the effectiveness of Israel's air defence capabilities.

stories.title: Aid flotilla reaches Cuba amid US oil blockade and blackouts
stories.summary: An aid flotilla has arrived in Cuba as a US oil blockade has caused severe fuel shortages and widespread power outages across the island nation.

stories.title: Iranian IRGC’s ties to Hezbollah deepen tensions in Lebanese politics
stories.summary: Lebanon's prime minister stated that Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) is directing Hezbollah's operations, with analysts confirming Iranian influence over the group's decisions in Lebanese politics.

stories.title: Israeli strike hits Tyre during Al Jazeera report
stories.summary: An Israeli missile struck a waterfront building in the Lebanese city of Tyre, interrupting a live Al Jazeera broadcast from the location.

stories.title: Moment rescuers find man alive under the rubble in Tehran
stories.summary: Rescue workers in Tehran recovered a man alive from rubble following US-Israeli strikes that hit a residential area in the Iranian capital.

stories.title: UN experts urge Israel to free Gaza doctor amid reports of ‘severe torture’
stories.summary: UN special rapporteurs called on Israel to release detained Gaza doctor Hussam Abu Safia, stating he has been systematically denied medical treatment and alleging severe torture during his detention.

stories.title: Philippines declares energy emergency over Iran conflict
stories.summary: Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr declared an energy emergency, citing imminent danger to the country's energy supplies caused by the ongoing conflict involving Iran.

stories.title: Keir Starmer’s policy on the Iran war is a recipe for catastrophe
stories.summary: The British government's policy on the Iran war has drawn criticism for allegedly repeating mistakes made during the US-UK invasion of Iraq.

stories.title: QatarEnergy declares force majeure on some LNG contracts due to Iran war
stories.summary: QatarEnergy declared force majeure on certain liquefied natural gas contracts due to production disruptions linked to the US-Israeli military operations against Iran.

stories.title: Is the US talking to Iran’s Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, and who is he?
stories.summary: Iranian officials, including parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, have denied reports that negotiations with the United States are taking place.

stories.title: Why has India arrested US, Ukrainian nationals under ‘anti-terror’ laws?
stories.summary: Indian authorities arrested six Ukrainian nationals and one American citizen under anti-terrorism laws, alleging they crossed from India into Myanmar to train armed groups in drone warfare.

stories.title: Search for four missing soldiers after Colombia plane crash kills 66
stories.summary: A Colombian military Hercules transport plane crashed shortly after takeoff near the country's southern border with Peru, killing 66 people, with search operations ongoing for four missing soldiers.

stories.title: Elon Musk's Starlink blocked from operating in Namibia
stories.summary: Namibia's telecommunications regulator blocked Elon Musk's Starlink satellite internet service from operating in the country, citing that Starlink's subsidiary does not meet local ownership requirements.

stories.title: Inside the alleged Russian operation to trigger anti-government protests in Angola
stories.summary: A group of Russian and Angolan nationals are facing trial in Angola on charges of allegedly organizing anti-government protests, accusations which the defendants deny.

stories.title: UK universities flock to India - but will they succeed?
stories.summary: Nine UK universities are establishing campuses in India, though initial student enrollment is expected to remain modest.

stories.title: Oil falls and shares rebound after Trump says talks have been held to end war
stories.summary: Global oil prices declined and stock markets recovered after US President Trump announced that productive talks had been held regarding ending the ongoing war.

stories.title: A committed pharmacist and a homesick blogger – the Iranian civilians killed in the war
stories.summary: Civilian casualties continue to rise in Iran as the US-Israeli military campaign progresses, with victims including a pharmacist and a blogger among those killed.

stories.title: Ex-teacher accused of Scotland school abuse found guilty of sex attack in South Africa
stories.summary: A court in Cape Town found Iain Wares, a former teacher accused of abuse at a Scottish school, guilty of indecently assaulting a former student who alleged sexual abuse occurred in the 1980s.

stories.title: Could Iranian missiles reach London and Paris?
stories.summary: Experts suggest Iran may possess missiles capable of reaching London, but such missiles would likely be intercepted before arrival and the overall risk is considered low.

stories.title: US' and Iran's options for ending war narrow the longer it goes on
stories.summary: The ongoing conflict between the US and Iran shows no signs of resolution, with Iran refusing to back down and US air power alone proving insufficient to achieve its primary objectives.

stories.title: Blast that injured two was 'terrorist attack', Ukrainian authorities say
stories.summary: Ukrainian authorities have classified a blast that injured two people as a terrorist attack. The suspect, a 21-year-old local resident, claims he was blackmailed and coerced into planting the explosives.

stories.title: Australia's ABC staff to go on strike for first time in 20 years
stories.summary: Staff at Australia's ABC are set to strike for 24 hours, marking the first such industrial action at the broadcaster in 20 years, with disruptions expected to live television and radio programming.

stories.title: Germany has a shortage of workers - so it's turning to India for help
stories.summary: Germany is recruiting skilled workers from India to address its domestic labor shortage.

stories.title: France's Socialists hold on to power in major cities in election boost for mainstream
stories.summary: France's Socialist Party retained control of Paris and Marseille in local elections, while the nationalist right won in Nice and several other towns.

stories.title: Israeli settlers target Palestinian villages in occupied West Bank, attacking people and properties
stories.summary: Israeli settlers attacked Palestinian villages and properties in the occupied West Bank following the death of 18-year-old settler Yehuda Sherman, who was reportedly struck by a Palestinian-driven vehicle while on his quad bike.

stories.title: National blackout hits Cuba for second time in a week
stories.summary: Cuba experienced its second nationwide power grid failure in a week, highlighting the country's ongoing hardships amid a US fuel blockade.

stories.title: Why did US and Israel attack Iran and how long could the war last?
stories.summary: Military conflict has expanded across the Middle East following US and Israeli strikes on Iran launched on 28 February.

stories.title: Israel to expand ground and air attacks against Hezbollah in Lebanon
stories.summary: Israel has announced plans to expand ground and air operations against Hezbollah in Lebanon, raising fears of a large-scale ground invasion.

stories.title: Iranian missiles injure 180 in towns near Israeli nuclear site
stories.summary: Iranian ballistic missiles injured 180 people in towns near an Israeli nuclear site, prompting Israel to investigate how the missiles penetrated its air defense systems.

stories.title: Qatari and Turkish citizens die in military helicopter crash
stories.summary: A military helicopter crash killed seven people, including four Qatari military personnel, one Turkish serviceman, and two technicians from a Turkish defense company.

stories.title: 'It's been bittersweet': The Iranian-Iraqi cafe drawing crowds to Hackney
stories.summary: Logma, a newly opened Iranian-Iraqi cafe in Hackney, London, has gained viral popularity for its sandwiches.

stories.title: 'Peace is a gradual thing': How land, cattle and identity fuel a deadly Nigerian conflict
stories.summary: Ongoing violence in Nigeria's Plateau state is fueled by disputes over land, cattle, and identity, compounded by a lack of justice and distrust in security forces.

stories.title: Trump at a crossroads as US weighs tough options in Iran
stories.summary: President Trump's statements that the war with Iran is nearly over contradict the ongoing situation on the ground.

stories.title: Why there's no sign of the conflict in the Middle East 'winding down'
stories.summary: Iran's foreign minister stated that the US does not appear ready to halt its aggression, despite President Trump's comments about potentially winding down the war.

stories.title: US lifts sanctions on some Iranian oil as energy prices soar
stories.summary: The US Treasury Secretary announced the lifting of some sanctions on Iranian oil, a move expected to bring approximately 140 million barrels of oil to global markets amid rising energy prices.

stories.title: UK allows US to use bases to strike Strait of Hormuz targets
stories.summary: The UK government approved the use of British military bases by the US to conduct strikes on targets in the Strait of Hormuz, with Downing Street citing Iran's "reckless strikes" as justification.

stories.title: BTS Arirang review: K-pop idols rekindle their fire
stories.summary: BTS released their 10th studio album, Arirang, which marks a return to the rap-heavy, rebellious style of their earlier music.

stories.title: Russia's school propaganda was  highlighted by Oscar-winning film - but does it work?
stories.summary: An Oscar-winning film highlighted Russia's school propaganda efforts, which portray the full-scale invasion of Ukraine as a defensive war and equate patriotism with unquestioning loyalty.

stories.title: The forgotten Indian woman trailblazer in British medicine
stories.summary: In 1912, Jamini Sen became the first woman to be granted Fellowship at Glasgow's Royal College, an institution founded in 1599 that had previously excluded women.

stories.title: Iranian strikes on bases used by US caused $800m in damage, new analysis shows
stories.summary: New analysis reveals that Iranian strikes on bases used by US forces caused approximately $800 million in damage, with much of the destruction occurring during Iran's initial retaliatory attacks following a US-Israeli operation.

stories.title: Ukraine-Hungary oil pipeline row threatens EU loan
stories.summary: Ukraine and Hungary are in dispute over the extent of damage to an oil hub in western Ukraine that was bombed by Russia, with the disagreement threatening an EU loan as oil flow through the pipeline remains suspended.

stories.title: Car stolen with two-month-old baby inside
stories.summary: Police rescued an unharmed two-month-old baby boy and reunited him with his mother shortly after the infant was inside a car when it was stolen.

stories.title: Venezuelan leader replaces senior military commanders
stories.summary: Venezuelan leader Delcy Rodríguez replaced senior military commanders, including appointing a new defence minister, a move that human rights groups characterized as a "recycling of impunity."

stories.title: Trump makes Pearl Harbor remark in meeting with Japan's PM
stories.summary: During a meeting with Japan's Prime Minister, President Trump compared US military strikes on Iran to Japan's 1941 attack on Pearl Harbor.

stories.title: Colombia's budding tech scene needs a cash boost
stories.summary: Colombia has emerged as a technology hub for Latin America but continues to face challenges in attracting investment to sustain its growing tech sector.

stories.title: Desperate for food, drought-stricken Kenyans turn to the gingerbread tree
stories.summary: Approximately 26 million people in Kenya, Ethiopia, and Somalia are facing extreme hunger due to drought conditions, according to Oxfam, leading Kenyans to turn to gingerbread trees as a food source.

stories.title: Watch: Sean Penn receives 'Oscar' in Ukraine after skipping US ceremony
stories.summary: Academy Award-winning actor Sean Penn, who won his third Oscar on Sunday, skipped the US ceremony and instead traveled to Ukraine where he received the award.

stories.title: Young Venezuelans voice hope and frustration as post-Maduro future unfolds
stories.summary: Young Venezuelans are adapting to political change following the seizure of former President Maduro by US forces, having previously experienced only one political system throughout their lives.

stories.title: 'Fire came from the sky and burned them' - life on the brink of civil war in South Sudan
stories.summary: Approximately 50,000 people in South Sudan's Jonglei state have been ordered to evacuate their homes after the military announced plans for a major offensive in the region.

stories.title: Fifa sanctions Nigeria and DR Congo over World Cup play-off
stories.summary: FIFA has issued fines to both the Nigeria Football Federation and the DR Congo Football Association due to separate disciplinary violations committed by their supporters during World Cup play-off matches.

stories.title: Wary allies show there's no quick fix to Trump's Iran crisis
stories.summary: European leaders are showing reluctance to assist the Trump administration in securing the Strait of Hormuz amid the ongoing Iran conflict, though they acknowledge that remaining uninvolved is not a viable option.

stories.title: How Iranians are evading internet blocks to contact family abroad
stories.summary: Iranian citizens are using various technological methods to circumvent government-imposed restrictions on phone and internet services in order to communicate with family members living abroad.

stories.title: Will Trump help or hinder Zimbabwe's white farmers in their compensation battle?
stories.summary: White farmers in Zimbabwe seeking compensation have hired a lobbying firm with connections to US President Trump to advocate for their case.

stories.title: Under drone fire, exiled Kurds wait to confront Iranian regime
stories.summary: Kurdish fighters exiled in Iraq report they are prepared to return to Iran while continuing to face drone attacks launched by Tehran.

stories.title: Iranians react to new supreme leader's first address
stories.summary: Iranians are expressing uncertainty about the country's leadership following new supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei's first public address, which was delivered through a presenter on state television rather than directly.

stories.title: As hopes of regime change in Iran fade, Netanyahu faces political test
stories.summary: Israeli leaders are presenting their bombing campaign against Iran as a strategic success that has reshaped the Middle East in Israel's favor, as Prime Minister Netanyahu faces growing pressure to end the conflict.

stories.title: 'There's no hiding place on a ship': The sailors stranded near Iran
stories.summary: Sailors stranded on ships in the Gulf region are regularly witnessing military activity including drones, cruise missiles, and fighter jets amid the ongoing Iran conflict.

stories.title: Mission accomplished? The 2003 boast that haunts today's Iran conflict
stories.summary: Analysts are drawing comparisons between the current Iran conflict and the 2003 Iraq War, noting both similarities and significant differences between the two military campaigns.

stories.title: 'Follow the smoke': BBC spends day with emergency teams as Israel strikes south Lebanon
stories.summary: BBC journalists accompanied emergency response teams in the southern Lebanese city of Nabatieh, documenting Israeli airstrikes as the conflict between Israel and Hezbollah intensifies.

stories.title: Tracking the wave of ship attacks that has choked off Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Six ships have reportedly been attacked in the Gulf within a 48-hour period, bringing the total number of vessels targeted during the ongoing war to 18 and severely disrupting traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: 'What if we're left with ruins?': Doubts creep in for Iranians who supported war
stories.summary: Iranian citizens who initially supported the war, including teachers, engineers, and shopkeepers, are now expressing concerns to the BBC about the potential for their country to descend into chaos.

stories.title: Trump sets his sights on crisis-hit Cuba after Iran action
stories.summary: US President Trump has turned attention to Cuba following military action in Iran, claiming Cuban authorities are eager to negotiate a deal with the United States.

stories.title: Flying oranges: Italian town celebrates carnival with historic street battle
stories.summary: The town of Ivrea in northern Italy has begun its annual carnival celebration featuring the Battle of the Oranges, a historic tradition in which participants throw oranges at each other in a large-scale street battle.
